info.name: DRIVMAN Backend API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the DRIVMAN backend.

## How to use
1. Import BOTH this collection and `DRIVMAN.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the **DRIVMAN Local** environment (top-right dropdown).
3. Run the folders **in order**: 01 Health -> 02 Auth -> 03 Catalog -> 04 Wishlist -> 05 Cart -> 06 Addresses -> 07 Orders -> 08 Admin.

Tokens, product ids and order ids are captured automatically into environment variables by each request's Tests script, so you never need to copy/paste an id.

## Notes
- Signup does NOT return a token. You must verify the email first.
- In development the verification/reset tokens are returned in the response body as `devVerificationToken` / `devResetToken` so you can test without opening a mailbox.
- With Twilio unset, OTP login uses the dev code `123456`.

request.description: Confirms the server is running. Run this first — if it fails, nothing else will work.

item.name: 02 · Auth
item.description: Full authentication flow. Run top-to-bottom the first time.

request.description:
Creates an UNVERIFIED account and emails a 6-digit verification code.

Returns NO token — you cannot log in until the email is verified.
In development the code is echoed back as `devOtpCode` and captured automatically.

If the code cannot be sent, the account is deleted so the address isn't locked up.

exec: console.warn("No devOtpCode — is NODE_ENV=production? Read the code from the inbox.");

request.description: Proves the verification gate works. This SHOULD fail with 403.

Alias of POST /api/auth/email/send-otp — kept so existing clients keep working.

Always returns the same generic message so it can't be used to discover which emails are registered.

Per-email limits: 1 per 60s, 5 per hour. Also IP-limited to 10/hour.
Expect 429 if you run this right after signup — that is the cooldown working.

exec: console.log("Cooldown active — expected within 60s of the last request.");

request.description:
Confirms the address with the 6-digit code and logs you straight in — returns both tokens.

The code is single-use, expires in 10 minutes, and dies after 5 wrong guesses.

Sends a login OTP by SMS.

With Twilio unconfigured the server runs in DEV mode: the code is always `123456` and is printed to the server console.
Third login method. Use the code from the previous request (dev default: 123456).

Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token.

The refresh token is ROTATED — the old one stops working immediately. Always save the new one.

Keeps THIS device logged in and revokes every other session.

After running this, update the `userPassword` environment variable to `NewPassw0rd1`.
Emails a reset link valid for 15 minutes. Generic response regardless of whether the email exists.
Sets a new password and revokes ALL sessions on every device.
Sends an OTP to the logged-in user's registered number, to mark the phone as verified.

item.name: 03 · Catalog (Categories & Products)
item.description: Public browsing endpoints — no authentication required.

request.description: All 10 car makes: Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai, Kia, Tata, Mahindra, Toyota, Honda, Volkswagen, Skoda, MG.
Nested form — root categories with their children populated.
Also works with an id. Includes a live `productCount`.
Paginated. Response includes `meta` with page/limit/total/totalPages.
Partial, case-insensitive match across name, brand, vehicleModel and description.
Accepts a category slug or id. Includes child categories automatically.
pieces = SET OF PCS from your price list. rows = seating rows (3-row / 4-row with dicky).
Options: newest, oldest, price_asc, price_desc, name_asc, name_desc, rating.
Distinct brand list — useful for building filter dropdowns.
Returns the product plus up to 8 `related` products from the same category.
Idempotent — adding the same product twice returns `alreadyPresent: true` rather than erroring.
Adds to the cart and removes from the wishlist in one call.

item.name: 05 · Cart
item.description:
Requires a logged-in, email-verified user.

Prices are always read live from the product — the cart never stores a price.

request.description: Returns items with live prices, per-line subtotals and a summary block.
Adding a product already in the cart INCREMENTS its quantity. Max 10 per product, capped by stock.
Sets an ABSOLUTE quantity (not a delta). Sending 0 removes the line.
Changing the phone number resets `isPhoneVerified` to false.
The first address saved automatically becomes the default.

Deleting the default promotes the next address automatically.

Note: this clears `addressId`; folder 07 creates a fresh address of its own.

item.name: 07 · Orders
item.description:
Checkout flow.

The first two requests set up an address and a cart item, so this folder runs standalone.

request.description: Guarantees a valid address exists for the orders below, regardless of what folder 06 left behind.
Guarantees the cart is non-empty before checkout.

Sources line items from your cart, reserves stock atomically, and clears the cart.

COD orders are `confirmed` immediately.

You can pass a full `shippingAddress` object instead of `addressId`.

item.name: Create order — COD with inline address

request.description: Guest-style checkout — no saved address needed.
Passing `items` bypasses the cart entirely and leaves it untouched.

Creates a pending order plus a Razorpay order.

The response `payment` block gives you `razorpayOrderId`, `amount`, `currency` and `keyId` to hand to the Razorpay checkout widget.

Returns 400 if RAZORPAY_KEY_ID / RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET are not set.

Call this after the Razorpay widget succeeds.

Paste the `razorpay_payment_id` and `razorpay_signature` the widget returns. The server verifies the HMAC before marking the order paid — a forged signature is rejected.

item.name: List my orders — filter by status

request.description: Takes a UI bucket (placed, shipped, out_for_delivery, delivered, cancelled) or a raw status (pending, confirmed, processing, shipped, out_for_delivery, delivered, cancelled).
Allowed only before dispatch. Restores stock automatically. Paid orders move to `refunded`.

item.name: 08 · Admin
item.description:
Requires an account with `role: "admin"`.

Create one with: `npm run seed:fresh` (creates admin@drivman.com / Admin@12345), then run **Admin login** first to populate `adminAccessToken`.

request.description: Saves the token into `adminAccessToken` — every request in this folder uses it.
The slug is generated from the name automatically.
Refuses to delete while products or subcategories still reference it.

request.description: Sets isActive=false so existing orders keep resolving. Add `?hard=true` to remove permanently.
Categories, brands, colours, vehicleTypes, badges, sort keys and upload limits — populate the Add/Edit Product form from this instead of hardcoding values.
Management list. Includes hidden products, and returns a catalog-wide `summary` for the header count and filter chips.

exec: pm.test("has meta + summary", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.meta.page).to.eql(1); pm.expect(d.summary.total).to.be.a("number"); });

item.name: Products list — search by name or SKU

request.description: One `search` box covers product name, SKU, brand and car model.
Accepts a category id or slug; includes the category's direct children.

item.name: Products list — filter by stock bucket

request.description: all | in | low | out. Buckets are mutually exclusive: out = 0, low = 1…LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD, in = above it.
status = all | visible | hidden.
Loads a product for the edit form even when it is hidden — the public endpoint 404s on those.

formdata.description: Up to 6 files, 5MB each (JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF). First one becomes the main photo.

request.description: Every field in the Add Product form. `sku` is auto-generated from brand + car model when omitted.
Backs the VISIBLE / HIDDEN switch. Send an empty body to flip the current value.

query.description: all | placed | shipped | out_for_delivery | delivered | cancelled
Order number, order id, customer or recipient name/email/phone

request.description: The admin order table. Returns `orders`, `meta` and `summary.statuses` — the per-bucket counts that drive the status dropdown.
Status counts plus bookedRevenue, collectedRevenue and awaitingPayment. Accepts the same filters as /admin/all.

Forward-only state machine:
pending -> confirmed -> processing -> shipped -> out_for_delivery -> delivered

`shipped` may go straight to `delivered` when the courier reports no out-for-delivery scan. Any state up to `processing` can also go to `cancelled` (which restores stock). Marking a COD order `delivered` also marks it paid.

Customers table: role=user only, each row carries ordersCount/totalSpent. Optional filters: status (all|active|blocked), search (name/email/phone), sort (newest|oldest|name_asc|name_desc). Response includes summary with header-tile counts.
Optional filters: role, search (matches name/email/phone).
Body may be {isActive}, {blocked}, or {} to flip the current state (what the table's block icon sends). Blocking revokes sessions immediately. Response includes the refreshed summary tiles.
Codes are uppercased automatically. Omit `usageLimit` / `expiresAt` for unlimited / never-expires.
Every row carries a derived `status`, `remainingUses` and `isExpired` for the admin table.
`status` ∈ active | inactive | expired | exhausted | all
The same endpoint accepts an id or the code itself.
Backs the toggle switch in the coupons table.
Uses the normal user's token — the whole /api/coupons router is admin-only.
A coupon that has been redeemed is protected — pass `?force=true` to delete it anyway.

item.name: 09 · Security & Validation checks
item.description: These SHOULD fail — they prove the guards work.

request.description: Ensures the checks below run as a NORMAL user, not an admin.

Sends neither an Authorization header nor an auth cookie.

Note: the API accepts EITHER a Bearer token or the httpOnly cookie. Postman keeps cookies from earlier logins, so this request clears them in a pre-request script — otherwise the cookie would legitimately authenticate it.

exec: // Clear auth cookies so this request truly carries no credentials.

request.description: Uses the normal-user token captured above. MUST be 403.
Phone must be E.164: +91XXXXXXXXXX
5 consecutive failures lock the account for 15 minutes.

item.name: 10 · Logout (run last)
item.description: Kept in its own folder at the end — running these mid-collection would revoke the token every later request needs.

request.description: Revokes this device's refresh token and clears the auth cookies.
Proves the refresh token was really revoked.
Log in again first if you want to test this — the previous request already ended the session.

item.name: 11 · Email OTP (verification codes)
item.description:
Exercises the email verification code flow on its own, including the abuse protections.

Run AFTER folder 02 (needs a signed-up account). These use a throwaway address
so they do not disturb the main test user's state.

request.description: An address with no account returns exactly the same body as a registered one, and no email is sent. This is what stops the endpoint being used to discover who is registered.

exec: pm.test("Generic message", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("If that email is registered"));
// No devOtpCode: nothing was dispatched, because there is no account.
pm.test("No code issued for an unknown address", () => pm.expect(b.data.devOtpCode).to.be.undefined);

request.description:
The per-email cooldown is 1 request per 60 seconds, enforced in MongoDB so it survives a restart.

It applies to unknown addresses too — otherwise the 429 itself would reveal which addresses exist.

exec: pm.test("Says how long to wait", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.match(/wait \d+ second/i));

request.description: Every failure — wrong code, expired code, no code requested, unknown address — returns this one identical message. Distinguishing them would leak which accounts exist.

exec: pm.test("Generic failure message", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include("invalid or has expired"));

item.name: 4. Burn 4 more guesses, then expect lockout (429)

request.description:
Five wrong guesses kill the code — a fresh request is then required.

This request loops itself 4 times using postman.setNextRequest, so the 5th attempt (counting the previous request) trips the lockout.

exec: // Attempt 2..5 of the 5-guess budget; attempt 5 must lock out.
postman.setNextRequest("4. Burn 4 more guesses, then expect lockout (429)");
pm.test("5th wrong guess locks the code (429)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(429));
pm.test("Tells the user to request a new code", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.match(/request a new code/i));
